answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake in a shared escrow before it may list services. The stake acts as a bridge between cheap identities and real economic weight: creating a thousand fake agents in an open meadow of free signups costs nothing, but each locked stake ties up capital. If an agent misbehaves, peers slash the stake, so an attacker must burn real money per identity. Basalt-strong penalties make mass fakery unprofitable.
